what_its_for: Protriptyline is an antidepressant used to treat depression. It belongs to a group of medicines called tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs). It works by balancing certain natural chemicals in your brain that affect your mood.
how_to_take: Take protriptyline by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a small snack or meal. Do not crush or chew the tablets — swallow them whole. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Because this medicine can keep you awake, your doctor may tell you to take your last dose in the early afternoon rather than at bedtime.
dosing: The usual adult starting dose is 5 mg to 10 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose up to a maximum of 60 mg per day. Older adults usually start at a lower dose of 5 mg taken 3 times a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — never take more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is well before your next scheduled dose. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store protriptyline at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine — it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and may worsen side effects. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid standing up too quickly, as this medicine can lower your blood pressure and cause dizziness or fainting. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and tanning beds, as this medicine may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight — use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Tell your doctor before taking any other medicines, including over-the-counter drugs and herbal supplements, especially MAO inhibitors (like phenelzine or tranylcypromine) — combining these can be life-threatening.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: thoughts of suicide or self-harm, worsening depression or anxiety, unusual changes in mood or behavior, chest pain or irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness or fainting, difficulty urinating, eye pain or vision changes, seizures, or signs of a severe allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Contact your doctor if you have dry mouth, constipation, blurred vision, or trouble sleeping that does not go away, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
when_it_works: Protriptyline may start to improve your sleep, appetite, and energy levels within the first 1 to 2 weeks. However, it may take 2 to 4 weeks — or sometimes up to 6 weeks — before you notice a full improvement in your mood and depression symptoms. Do not stop taking this medicine even if you feel better, unless your doctor tells you to. Stopping suddenly can cause withdrawal symptoms.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with caution. Older patients are more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness, confusion, constipation, and urinary problems. A lower starting dose is usually recommended. Children and teenagers: This medicine is not generally recommended for children. Antidepressants may increase the risk of suicidal thoughts in children, teenagers, and young adults — especially in the first few weeks of treatment. Close monitoring is very important. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The risks and benefits need to be discussed with your doctor before using this medicine. Heart conditions: Tell your doctor if you have any heart problems, as this medicine can affect your heart rhythm. Glaucoma or prostate problems: Use with caution, as this medicine may worsen these conditions.
